anchors.code: fw2 = fu_bytes_new_offset(payload, offset_tmp, payloadsz - offset_tmp, error);
anchors.note: With `offset_tmp` at 0 on the first and only loop iteration, `fw2` aliases the full 15-byte coSWID payload and becomes the object passed to `fu_firmware_parse()`.
Inside `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()`, the inner parser rereads all bytes from `fw2` into local `fw`, carrying the same 15-byte payload forward.
The 15-byte payload is materialized as the CBOR map `{2:{33:[9,1,1,2,1,4]}}`. Root tag 2 (`ENTITY`) is the only top-level tag, so parsing proceeds into `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()`.
parse_entity allocates a 40-byte `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` with `g_new0`, so `entity->roles[0..5]` start as six `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` zero sentinels.
For tag 33 (`ROLE`), `pairs[i].value` is the six-element array `[9,1,1,2,1,4]`. `cbor_array_size(pairs[i].value)` is 6, exactly matching the six-slot `roles` buffer, and every element is nonzero.

Before each array write, the only capacity guard is `entity_role_cnt >= G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)`. It stays false on iterations 0 through 5, including the final write into `roles[5]`, and therefore does not reserve room for a zero terminator.

On the sixth iteration, this store writes the last nonzero role `4` into `entity->roles[5]`; together with the earlier stores `9,1,1,2,1`, the in-bounds buffer becomes `[9,1,1,2,1,4]` with no remaining `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` sentinel.
The entity carrying the fully nonzero `roles[0..5]` buffer is retained in `priv->entities`, so the later serialization path reuses this same heap object.
During reserialization, `fu_coswid_firmware_write()` retrieves that stored entity back from `priv->entities` into local `entity`.
Sink step. The loop condition itself reads `entity->roles[j]`; because slots 0 through 5 are all nonzero, the evaluation for `j == 6` performs the saved 4-byte read just past the 40-byte allocation.

anchors.note: Source. This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled embedded coSWID payload from the uSWID wrapper into project state.

Root cause. On the witnessed sixth loop iteration, this store writes the last attacker-controlled nonzero role into `roles[5]`. Together with the earlier five nonzero stores, that exhausts the six-slot sentinel-terminated array and leaves no in-bounds `FU_COSWID_ENTITY_ROLE_UNKNOWN` entry for the later write-side scan. The patch fixes this by switching to a bitfield and rejecting invalid role values before setting it.
Project-side sink. Evaluating this loop condition on the stored six-value role array reads `entity->roles[6]` past the 40-byte `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` allocation.
